title: Chess, But Each Piece Gets Only 5 Moves
summary: Tony plays chess where each of his pieces can move only five times before it becomes immobile (a red bubble on each piece counts 5→0). He throws pawns forward as 'grenades' (a pawn that promotes uses its 5th move and the new queen is stuck forever), saves queen/rook moves for the mating attack, and beats Martin (game 1, double check mate ~3:19) and then Martin's 'cousin' Smartin (game 2, Nh6# ~11:45).
rules: Every one of the player's pieces starts with 5 moves; each move with that piece decrements its red badge (5,4,3,2,1,0).
A piece at 0 can no longer move at all (it still blocks and can be captured).
The counter travels with the piece; a pawn that promotes on its 5th move becomes a queen with 0 moves left (permanently immobile).
Frame sprite shows the KING also wears a move-counter badge (showing 1), so the king is NOT exempt (inferred from frame; transcript does not state a king exception).
Castling counts as a king move (Tony castles at 4:53; inferred it uses the king's counter).
Opponent bots appear to move freely (Smartin's king shuffles repeatedly late in game 2); whether the bot is also limited is not stated (inferred: limit applies to the player only).
win_condition: Checkmate the bot. Two games: Martin then Smartin.
